title: Time Helix
program_note:
Time Helix portrays the spiral passage of time—where certain events recur or seem to recur, and yet, given the inexorable march forward through time, nothing is precisely the same:  themes are subtly altered, or the colors change and evolve.  Thus, the music never repeats itself, but it does rhyme!
The three main thematic elements of the music are heard within the first minute and a half:  the main theme, presented boldly in the brass right at the outset, the slowly-cycling ever-rising lines, first heard in the low strings, and the more expressive (melancholic?) theme, first heard somewhat later, stated in the oboe and English horn with countermelodies starting in the first violins.  All of the material is subject to “helical repetitions”—modified re-presentations, canons, and time-stretches, some of which manifest as being in different meters.  These helical repetitions multiply the numbers of layers until, in the middle of the three broad sections of the piece, the many rising lines are compressed into just two or three compound rising lines.  On top of this thinner texture are heard what might be termed “jazz solos,” formed out of the motives and themes of the first section.  These jazz solos get evened out and transformed into a quasi-minimalistic texture, heard in the hushed woodwinds, against which is found a swelling, rising line in the strings.  This returns to the opening texture—but with the rising lines now in the high strings—in the last of the three broad sections.  Here the time stretches of helical repetitions become even more exaggerated (and sometimes blurred, as if heard from a great distance), culminating in a slow presentation in the lowest instruments (contrabassoon, tubas, string basses) against the violins near the top of their register.
Time Helix is about 9 minutes in duration.

David S. Lefkowitz
Los Angeles, CA
27 September, 2019
